answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may bid for work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fabricated results or collusion. A genuine agent earns the lock back through repeated verified jobs; a sybil operator must fund every persona separately and risks losing those deposits, so multiplying identities becomes costly rather than free. A relic registry can record slashes, while a jetty of reviewers checks evidence and a lotus-shaped score weights reliability across tasks.
